title: `onError` hook is called before `setErrorHandler`
body:
### Prerequisites

- [x] I have written a descriptive issue title
- [x] I have searched existing issues to ensure the bug has not already been reported


### Fastify version

5.3.1

### Plugin version

_No response_

### Node.js version

20.11.1

### Operating system

macOS

### Operating system version (i.e. 20.04, 11.3, 10)

15.5

### Description

According to documentation [Reply lifecycle](https://fastify.dev/docs/latest/Reference/Lifecycle/#reply-lifecycle) and `onError`:
> This hook will be executed only after the [Custom Error Handler set by setErrorHandler](https://fastify.dev/docs/latest/Reference/Server/#seterrorhandler) has been executed, and only if the custom error handler sends an error back to the user (Note that the default error handler always sends the error back to the user).

However, in practice, the `onError` hook is always executed **before** the custom error handler.  
This causes `onError` to be triggered even for errors I intend to handle and respond to properly within my custom error handler, which results in misleading logging or error reporting.

Here is a minimal reproduction:
```javascript
import Fastify from 'fastify'

const fastify = await Fastify()

fastify.setErrorHandler((error, _req, reply) => {
  console.log('setErrorHandler')

  reply.status(400).send(error.message)
})

fastify.addHook('onError', async (_req, _reply, _error) => {
  console.log('onError')
})

fastify.get('/error', (_req, reply) => {
  reply.send(new Error('test error'))
})

await fastify.inject({
  method: 'GET',
  url: '/error',
})

// Console logs:
//   onError
//   setErrorHandler
```

I found a possibly related [issue](https://github.com/fastify/fastify/issues/5469) seems similar to what I'm observing here.

### Link to code that reproduces the bug

https://github.com/wongsean/reproduce-fastify-error-lifecycle

### Expected Behavior

`onError` hook should run after the custom error handler, and only if the custom error handler sends an error back to the user.
